title: Release safety chronicle (working notes)
content:
Quick context and intent:
- Personal scratchpad capturing the run-of-the-mill heuristics we keep retyping across canaries. Not official runbook yet; copy/paste into runbooks as needed.
- Goal: safely flip model or runtime image with predictable blast radius, fast rollback, and minimal manual babysitting.

High level release pattern (compact):
1) Preflight: infra + telemetry green, warmup plan baked, pin config staged.
2) Canary: 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% over ~3 windows (30m/30m/1h) with warmup cohorts + priming.
3) Observe: focused metric gates at each step (clear pass/fail predicates).
4) Rollforward to full (gradual) if gates hold; otherwise, immediate pinback and triage.

Important constraints / reminders:
- For inference model flips, cold-start token p95 can spike for first few minutes; don't treat isolated 1-2m blips as fatal unless sustained and correlated with error rate.
- Network region diversion: prefer diverting traffic away from a failing region rather than global rollback if isolated.
- When flipping quantized variants or kernel changes, expect error class shifts (e.g., hallucination/prompt-dep anomalies) — tie to prompt-driven evals.

Preflight checklist (execute ~2 hours before window):
- [ ] Confirm release image built and pushed. image-tag: release/2026-02-15-mc-1
- [ ] Smoke deploy to integration/stage cluster + sanity tests (text gen sanity, embedding dims, latency baseline).
- [ ] Instrumentation: traces and logs include new image tag and model_version metadata.
- [ ] Canary config staged in config service (pin lists for client cohorts).
- [ ] Alert paging rules tuned for canary noise (mute low severity alerts for first 10m of each window).
- [ ] Canary cohorts selected: internal-beta (employees), seed-pilot (low qps partners), public-tier-1 (low risk clients).
- [ ] Warmup prompts ready (10 prompts per domain; saved under GDrive: /templates/warmup-sets).

Cohort sequence and rationale:
- Warmup phase (5m) to pre-populate KV caches: send warmup prompts from internal-beta only. Confirm mem/cpu/gpu stable.
- Phase 1 (0.5% global): internal-beta + seed-pilot — sanity and edge-case catches.
- Phase 2 (2%): add a slice of public-tier-1; watch latency tail and error spike correlation.
- Phase 3 (10%): wider coverage, include longer sequences, and run regression prompt set; if good, proceed to 25% -> 50% -> full in subsequent windows (1–3h apart depending on traffic).

Metric gates (fail -> immediate pinback unless otherwise noted):
- Error rate (4xx/5xx / total requests) > 0.5% absolute increase over baseline for >5m = FAIL.
- Token-level latency: p95 > baseline_p95 * 1.5 for >10m = FAIL.
- Cost-per-token deviation: unexpected +20% sustained for 15m = investigate (don't auto-fail unless tied to quality).
- Quality regressions (measured via regression prompt set A/B): automated score drop > 3% absolute = FAIL.
- Model hallucination signal from production eval harness: flagged prompts > threshold (configurable) = FAIL.
- SRE health signals: pod restart rate > 0.5 restarts per pod per hour = FAIL.

Pinning notes and quick commands (for myself):
- To pin traffic back to stable: update config-service route: model_pin=stable_v2026-01-30 ; trigger rollout policy with immediate flag.
- If partial-region rollback: use routing override: region_override=us-west-2:stable_v2026-01-30.
- For emergency forced rollback: run emergency-pin script: /scripts/emergency_pin.sh --tag stable_v2026-01-30 --reason "canary-fail"; notify #release-alerts channel.

Warmup & priming heuristics (what to send):
- 10 short prompts per domain (chat start -> 4 tokens), 5 medium (50–100 tokens), 3 long (200+ tokens) — run across the cohort.
- Send edge-case known-failure prompts from historical incidents (search: confluence incident index).
- For KV-cache sensitive models, include partial conversation prefix to exercise cache reuse.

Observability playbook during windows (who watches what):
- Me (Maya): overall canary gate decisions and quality regression checks (regression harness scoreboard).
- Devon: infra & autoscaling watch (GPU utilization, pod churn).
- Ravi: logs/traces correlation and error class triage.
- Pager: SRE on-call (immediately notify if infra metrics cross thresholds).

Signals worth manual attention (not automatic gates):
- Sudden change in top error message text (new exception class) even if % low — might indicate silent degradation.
- Subtle hallucination increase on high-value prompts (finance/legal categories) — escalate to product.
- Downstream client complaints from partner slack — treat higher weight than automated noise.

Rollback vs. Pinback vs. Rollforward definitions (my shorthand):
- Pinback: change routing so clients hit previous model variant while the new deployment remains in cluster. Fast, low-change, default for errors.
- Rollback: redeploy previous image across cluster (slower, more heavy-handed). Use when pinback not possible or stateful incompatibility.
- Rollforward: apply a quick patch (e.g., config fix) and continue canary if issue is fixable without reverting. Only when fix confidence is high and fix validated in stage.

Triage checklist if a gate fires (first 30 minutes):
1) Capture immediate telemetry snapshot (p95, p50, errors, request rate, model_version breakdown).
2) Compare to baseline window (-24h same traffic slice).
3) Quick log sample of 100 failed requests to inspect error classes and prompts.
4) If infra-related -> region diversion or pinback. If model-quality related -> pinback + spawn product/ML convo.
5) Postmortem trigger decision: if outage > 30m or customer impact > threshold, open incident channel.

Notes on noisy metrics / false positives:
- During first 5–10m of each step we expect latency variance due to cache warmup and autoscaler cool-down. Only trigger if sustained beyond warmup window.
- Zero-day spikes in network latency should be correlated with cloud provider status page before flipping.

Loose TODOs and questions to resolve after canary:
- Automate the warmup job so it runs as part of canary windows (open ticket: JIRA-REL-4198).
- Make an easier UI for partial-region pinback in console (ask product).
- Clarify cost-gate action: investigation vs auto-fail threshold semantics.
- Run a tabletop for a multi-region partial failure scenario.

Notes-to-self (shortcuts, friction points):
- Avoid expanding cohorts during a lunch or late-night window. More human overlap = better.
- Keep a stable tag for emergency pinback that is rotated at release cadence (documented stable_vYYYY-MM-DD).
- If using quantized variant, leave a longer cool-down between phases; noise profile differs.

Historical reference (quick):
- 2025-06 canary: latency spike tied to kernel change; resolved by reverting kernel patch (pinback insufficient) — learned: kernel changes often require full rollback.
- 2025-09 model flip: hallucination regression detected at 2% window; pinback + extended regression harness saved us.

End of scratchpad. Revisit and move to shared runbook when stable.

Unresolved: what threshold to use for quality gate for small but high-value cohorts? flag for discussion with product in next release retrospective.

(Last quick note) Keep this doc lightweight and copy to confluence/rel-runbook as the canonical checklist once we align on final gate numbers.
